sources.entry: gonic - Lightweight music streaming server. Subsonic compatible. GPL-3.0 Go/Docker
gonic | Lightweight music streaming server implementing the Subsonic API

summary.one_liner: gonic is a lightweight, free-software music streaming server that implements the Subsonic API so Subsonic-compatible clients can browse and play a music library.
keywords: listen to my music collection from phone
summary.what_it_does: gonic is a Go implementation of the Subsonic API, letting Subsonic-compatible music clients connect to it. It can browse a music collection either by folder structure or by audio tags (via taglib, covering formats such as mp3, opus, flac, ape, m4a and wav). It supports on-the-fly transcoding with caching when ffmpeg is installed, and a jukebox mode that plays audio server-side via mpv. Multiple users can each have their own transcoding preferences, playlists and listening statistics. It also offers Last.fm and ListenBrainz scrobbling, podcast support, and a web interface for configuration and scans. Scanning can run at startup, on an interval, or via a filesystem watcher.
use_cases: stream a personal music collection to Subsonic-compatible apps
run a lightweight music server on a Raspberry Pi
browse music by folder or by tags
share a music library between several users
scrobble listening history to Last.fm or ListenBrainz
play music through a server-side jukebox
how_to_run: Install from source, Docker, or systemd (see the README's installation sections; details not expanded in the README text provided)
Set GONIC_MUSIC_PATH or pass -music-path to point at your music folder
Optionally set GONIC_CACHE_PATH, GONIC_PODCAST_PATH, GONIC_PLAYLISTS_PATH and GONIC_DB_PATH
Start gonic; it listens on 0.0.0.0:4747 by default
Log in to the web interface with admin/admin and change the password
notable: Browses by both folder tree and audio tags, with multi-valued genre and artist handling
Multiple music folders with ALIAS->PATH naming
Tested with many Subsonic clients including Symfonium, Amperfy, DSub and Sublime Music
Per-user transcoding preferences, playlists and top tracks/artists
Lightweight enough for a Raspberry Pi; ARM images are provided
caveats: Transcoding requires ffmpeg to be installed separately
Folder browsing expects all files of an album to sit in the same folder, and each folder to contain only one album
Default admin/admin credentials must be changed after first login
Delimiter-based multi-value tag splitting can produce false positives, per the README
